newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tutu threatens to quit S.Africa's truth commission.
newsitem.headline: Tutu threatens to quit S.Africa's truth commission.

text.p: Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu on Monday threatened to resign from South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission if the ruling African National Congress (ANC) refused to seek amnesty for past human rights abuses.

Tutu rejected the stance adopted by the ruling ANC's chief legal adviser, Mathews Phosa, who has said the party will not approach the state-funded commission for amnesty on the grounds that its fight against white rule was a "just struggle".
"If this position is accepted as ANC policy we will then have to look for another chairperson," Tutu told reporters in the Indian Ocean port city of Durban.
Tutu, popularly seen as South Africa's moral conscience, said the commission would serve no purpose if one side was to unilaterally declare itself blameless.
"If we allow the ANC... to get away with it, then people will justifiably say that the commission is a witch hunt by looking for people from only one side," he said.
Revelations before the truth commission have shown that the extra-judicial killing of government opponents during the 1980s was state-sanctioned, and not confined to renegade police units.
But tension is building over the failure of any individual ANC member to approach the commission for amnesty.
